title: Morning Light
style: English, indie folk, gentle female vocal, warm and breathy, acoustic guitar fingerpicking, upright bass and soft brushed drums, nostalgic tender, dry close-mic production, 98 BPM
lyrics:
[Intro]
Curtains breathe in
Dust turns gold on the sill

[Verse 1]
Your sweater's on the chair back, sleeves rolled twice
Kettle does that thing where it clicks before it boils
I cut the crust off your toast the way you like
Left the radio on the AM talk show
Something about the harvest, something about rain
The dog keeps nudging the screen door
Like the yard's got news for him
I stack the plates and don't rinse the honey jar

[Pre-Chorus]
And the clock on the stove is eleven minutes fast
Been eleven minutes fast since March
We never fixed it, never will
We just wake up early and call it ours

[Chorus]
Morning light, coming in sideways
Through the blinds we never closed
Morning light, on the dishes in the sink
On the floorboards, on your toes
I don't need a better day
I just need this one to hold
Morning light, morning light

[Verse 2]
You come down with your hair doing whatever it wants
Ask me what I dreamt, I say I don't remember
Half a truth, half a lie, the usual trade
There's a jar of pennies by the door
From the summer we drove out to the coast
And never counted a single one
You pour the milk, I read the sports page backwards
We let the crossword sit half done

[Pre-Chorus]
And the clock on the stove is eleven minutes fast
Been eleven minutes fast since March
We never fixed it, never will
We just wake up early and call it ours

[Chorus]
Morning light, coming in sideways
Through the blinds we never closed
Morning light, on the dishes in the sink
On the floorboards, on your toes
I don't need a better day
I just need this one to hold
Morning light, morning light

[Bridge]
One day this kitchen's gonna be somebody else's
Somebody else's toast, somebody else's kettle click
Somebody's kid will draw on this wallpaper
So I'm gonna stand right here a minute longer
Let the coffee go cold, let the coffee go cold

[Verse 3]
Outside the neighbor's mower coughs and quits
A truck backs up, the whole street knows the beep
You hum two bars of something I can't place
Then lose it, and it's gone for good
I put my hand flat on the warm countertop
And hold still like the room might move

[Outro]
Curtains breathe out
You're reading the back of the milk carton
I'm not going anywhere yet
Not yet
cover_prompt: soft indie folk morning, sunlit kitchen, dust in the air, linen and wood, 9:16 vertical
